articleTitle: Angular momentum of Airy beams under diffraction
abstract: The momentum and the density of the spin angular momentum of the electromagnetic field are found for a two-dimensional and three-dimensional elliptically polarized Airy beam in the first approximation in the angle of divergence. The choice of the beam is associated with its diffraction-free propagation in a homogeneous linear medium in the paraxial approximation. Due to this, diffraction effects appear only as corrections of the first order of smallness. For a linearly polarized beam, the appearance of the spin angular momentum is solely due to diffraction and is absent in the main order solution.

articleTitle: Accounting for modal excitability and bone porosity in ultrasonometric osteoporosis diagnostics
abstract: The present work is focused on the analytically based simulation of ultrasonic guided waves (GWs) piezo-electrically generated in samples mimicking waveguide properties of tubular bones. The studies are aimed to identify signs predicting osteoporosis. The developed computer models are based on the explicit GW representations in terms of the inverse Fourier transform path integrals of the waveguide’s Green matrix and the residue technique for GW extraction.

articleTitle: Computations of general Heun functions from their integral series representations
abstract: We present a numerical implementation of the recently developed unconditionally convergent representation of general Heun functions as integral series. We produce two codes in Python available for download, one of which is especially aimed at reproducing the output of Mathematica’s HeunG function. We show that the present code compares favorably with Mathematica’s HeunG and with an Oc- tave/Matlab code of Motygin, in particular when the Heun function is to be evaluated at a large number of points if less accuracy is sufficient. We suggest further improvements concerning the accuracy and discuss the issue of singularities.

articleTitle: Optimal control with phase constraints for a quasilinear endovenous laser ablation model
abstract: An optimal control problem for quasilinear equations of radiative-conductive heat transfer simulating the process of endovenous laser ablation in a bounded domain with the reflecting boundary is studied. In a given subdomain, it is required to provide a given temperature distribution, while the temperature in another given subdomain cannot exceed a critical value. On the basis of estimates of the solution of the controlled system, the solvability of the control problem is proved. An algorithm for solving the optimal control problem by minimizing the objective functional with a penalty is proposed. The eﬃciency of the algorithm is illustrated by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Rigorous mathematical formulation for quasiphotons. A priori estimates
abstract: An initial-boundary value problem is posed for the wave equation with a variable wave velocity in a half-plane on a semi-infinite time interval. The consideration is important for justification of a formula based on Poincaré wavelets that represents solutions to an initial-boundary value problem in the form of an integral superposition of elementary solutions (in particular, quasiphotons) depending on parameters. "Footprints" of quasiphotons at the boundary produce boundary data. We obtained a priori estimates of the dependence of solutions on parameters.

articleTitle: "Hybrid mode – linearly polarized optical vortex" transformation in multihelical optical fibers
abstract: We show that a multihelical optical fiber at certain parameters can be used for the high efficient transformation of EH- and HE-modes to linearly polarized optical vortices with topological charge +|ℓ| and –|ℓ|, respectively. We establish that the even EH- and HE-modes are transformed to the x-polarized optical vortices, while the odd ones are converted to the y-polarized optical vortices. This effect allows one to control the linear polarization of the optical vortex by controlling the parity of the hybrid mode and vice versa.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of unknown sources in the cerebral oxygen transport model
abstract: The analysis of an optimization algorithm for solving an inverse problem for the cerebral oxygen transport model is carried out. A theorem on the solvability of the optimal control problem is presented, an optimality system is constructed, and the convergence of approximate solutions to the solution of the inverse problem is proved. The results of numerical simulation are presented.

articleTitle: Hilbert spaces of functions associated with Jacobi matrices
abstract: We consider the dynamic problem for the discrete system with discrete time associated with (finite and semi-infinite) Jacobi matrices. The aim of the paper is to associate the special Hilbert spaces of functions, playing an important role in the inverse spectral theory, with these systems by making use of the method previously developed by the authors.

articleTitle: The boundary integral equation method for simulating guided waves scattering by a distribution of delaminations in a laminate
abstract: In the present study, the boundary integral equation method (BIEM) is extended to calculate eigenfrequencies and to simulate Lamb wave scattering by delaminations in laminates. The delaminations are modelled as a distribution of open micro-cracks and via the spring boundary conditions. The spatial-dependent spring boundary conditions are proposed to simulate a partially closed delamination, e.g. impact induced damage. The eigenfrequencies of a two-layer laminate made from dissimilar materials are calculated and analyzed for cases of uniform and non-uniform distributions of open micro-cracks.

articleTitle: Spectrum of Laplacians on periodic graphs with waveguides
abstract: We consider discrete Laplace operators on periodic graphs perturbed by guides, i.e., graphs that are periodic in some directions and finite in other ones. The spectrum of the Laplacian on the perturbed graphs consists of the spectrum of the Laplacian on the unperturbed periodic graph and the additional so-called guided spectrum which is a union of a finite number of bands. We determine sufficient conditions for the perturbations of the periodic graphs under which the guided bands appear in gaps of the unperturbed problem.

articleTitle: Hybrid numerical-analytical scheme for 3D scattering problems
abstract: Hybrid numerical-analytical approaches are currently being developed to obtain computationally efficient solutions based on linking the numerical solution in a local vicinity of the source and/or obstacles with an explicit analytical representation in the outer semi-infinite domain. However, the standard commercial FEM packages do not provide a direct opportunity for such a coupling. To avoid this limitation, a specific mathematical trick was invented and developed. The present paper gives examples of its extension to the case of 3D scattering.

articleTitle: Matching creeping waves with lit area diffraction field
abstract: We continue explorations of the shortwave plane wave diffraction for an axisymmetric elongated body. The previously obtained formulae for the boundary currents were evaluated numerically and showed matching in the borders of the regions going from the lit zone into the shadow. The results are presented for the cases of Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions.

articleTitle: Exact formulation of nonlocal transparent boundary conditions for elastic strip, plate, and cylinder
abstract: An elastic solid consisting of a certain core of finite size (Γ) and attached infinite solid (Ω) in the form of semi-strip, semi-cylinder, or 3D plate is considered. The harmonic time dependence is assumed and all possible energy sources are placed inside Γ. The exact non-reflecting boundary conditions (NBC) are suggested in the context of needs of nondestructive testing. Normally, Γ is the region of inspection and the impact of Ω is replaced by NBC providing the absence of waves coming from infinity. These NBC are obtained in the form of two singular and one hyper singular boundary integral equations on the contact surface Γ ∩ Ω. Thus, the total problem is reduced to the system of three ordinary boundary integral equations for region Γ with three additional NBC.

articleTitle: On the analogue of Kirchhoff’s formula for the wave equation in a two-dimensional domain
abstract: The subject of the paper is the Cauchy problem for the wave equation in a bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with data on ∂Ω × I, I ⊂ ℝ being a bounded time interval. We provide a regularizing algorithm for this problem, which is, in a sense, close to Kirchhoff’s formula. Note that the latter allows determining a solution from data on a bounded time interval only in odd dimensions.

articleTitle: Detection of small-scale inhomogeneities in an elastic-acoustic medium
abstract: The paper is devoted to the mathematical modeling of the plaques detection in the vein. Mathematically, we consider the problem of elastic-acoustic medium visualization. The visualization is conducted using Reverse time migration. Results of numerical experiments are presented.

articleTitle: A new concept of surface waves of the interference nature. Creeping waves
abstract: In this paper a new concept of the theory of creeping waves propagation along smooth, strictly convex surfaces imbedded in 3D Euclidian space is described. It is actually based on the extension of the locality principle, which is well known for short wave diffraction and propagation.

articleTitle: Study of the Doppler spectrum of surface reverberation using numerical simulation
abstract: We perform a numerical experiment to investigate how the surface reverberation spectrum changes with the intensity of the surface waves. We focus on the sound in the middle frequency range of 1 to 5 kHz, the scattering of which depends significantly on the state of the sea surface and may not be resonant. The novelty of this work is that we use an accurate diffraction model and a surface wave model that takes into account the nonlinear interaction between the surface harmonics.

articleTitle: Dispersion and attenuation of fundamental edge waves in a two-layered plate: 3D solution and approximate theories
abstract: Three-dimensional theory of elastodynamics is used to study fundamental edge waves (EW) in a two-layered plate composed of isotropic layers. It is shown that the second (extensional) EW subsides in its propagation along the edge because of coupling with the bending mode, carrying the energy away from the edge. The comparison of 3D solution with the results of classical laminated plate theory shows that the latter approximates dispersion curves of EW at low frequencies, but is inapplicable for describing of the attenuation. The model of a single layer with effective boundary conditions is tested for a plate, coated by a thin soft film, and turns out to be accurate in describing all the properties of EW including attenuation.

articleTitle: Diffraction of Gaussian beam by apertures and geometrical theory of diffraction
abstract: An application of geometrical theory of diffraction and physical optics method to solving scattering problem of Gaussian beam by circular aperture in a screen is discussed in the case of the short-wave approximation. An asymptotic analysis is developed to describe solution for the wave transmitted through the hole in the near-filed zone. Both asymptotic solutions for the point source and Gaussian beam diffraction were tested numerically to compute the transmitted wave field intensity versus the data obtained by the well-known approximation of the plane wave decomposition.

articleTitle: Formation of long strain waves in viscoelastic bar subjected to a longitudinal pulse load
abstract: A one-dimensional model for the plane longitudinal strain waves in a viscoelastic bar, which is valid for both long and short waves, is derived. This model consists of two coupled integro-differential equations. The model predictions for the largest strain wave are in good agreement with three-dimensional simulation and experimental results on the generation of a long strain wave by an impact on the bar’s edge.

articleTitle: Heun’s differential equation, integral transformation and q-deformation
abstract: We review some aspects of the Euler integral transformation for Heun’s differential equation and the deformed Heun equation (Heun1 equation). We introduce a q-deformation of the Heun equation and discuss a q-integral transformations for the q-Heun equation

articleTitle: Geoacoustic inversion of vertical line array data in shallow water with an ice cover
abstract: A technique for solving the inverse problem of estimating the effective acoustic parameters of the bottom is developed for shallow water with an ice cover. The initial data for the inversion are the experimental sound field amplitude at a vertical line array, and a set of precalculated dependences simulated for different effective bottom parameters. The range be-tween a sound source and the array is an order of magnitude higher that the water depth. In the calculations, the bottom is considered as a liquid homogeneous medium with different values of the sound speed, density, and attenuation coefficient. Numerical modelling is carried out within the framework of normal-mode theory. The obtained values of bottom parameters are considered effective if they provide a maximum agreement between experimental and simulated data. The technique has been tested in a field experiment on Lake Baikal with a solid ice cover.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of time-fractional diffusion-wave processes applied to communication in bacterial populations
abstract: The paper proposes a time-fractional diffusion-wave modification of the bacterial communication model to explore different dynamical regimes of the biological system. The model is formalized as an initialboundary value problem for a system of partial differential equations with Caputo time-fractional derivatives. A finite-difference implicit scheme coupled with an iterative procedure is constructed to solve the problem numerically. Computational experiments indicate realistic time-dependent fluctuations of signal compounds corresponding to the superdiffusion mode.

articleTitle: Light scattering by a spheroid. Relations between ‘spheroidal’ and ‘spherical’ T-matrices
abstract: Using the solution of the problem of light scattering by a homogeneous spheroid, derived by separation of variables in spheroidal coordinates, we find the ‘spheroidal’ T -matrix. We suggest a transformation of this matrix into the ‘spherical’ T -matrix useful in applications. The procedure consists of two steps: first, transition from spheroidal to spherical basis, and then from spherical non-orthogonal to orthogonal basis.

articleTitle: Parametrization of phase space of Painlevé V equation
abstract: All Painlevé equations can be considered as Hamiltonian systems. Their phase spaces are some algebraic symplectic manifolds. We consider the simplest Painlevé equation corresponding to the isomonodromic deformation of the differential system with irregular singularity. The presented theory explains the presence of the symplectic structure and gives a method of the canonical parametrization of the phase space.

articleTitle: Radiation resistance of a crossed-loop antenna in a magnetoplasma
abstract: Radiation resistance of an antenna in the form of two orthogonally crossed circular loops with quadrature-phased currents in a homogeneous magnetoplasma is studied using a rigorous approach based on an eigenfunction expansion representation of the excited field. The emphasis is on the analysis of the distribution of the radiated power over the spatial spectrum of the waves excited by such an antenna in the resonant part of the whistler frequency range under ionospheric conditions.

articleTitle: On linear cocycles over irrational rotations with secondary collisions
abstract: We consider a skew product F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf> = (σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ω</inf>,A) over irrational rotation ${\sigma _\omega }(x) = x + \omega $ of a circle ${\mathbb{T}^1}$. It is supposed that the transformation $A:{\mathbb{T}^1} \to SL(2,\mathbb{R})$, being a C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-map, has the form $A(x) = R(\varphi (x))Z(\lambda (x))$, where R(φ) is a rotation in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> over the angle φ and Z(λ) = diag{λ,λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>} is a diagonal matrix. Assuming that λ(x) ≥λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> > 1 with a sufficiently large constant λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> and the function φ is such that cos φ(x) possesses only simple zeroes, we study hyperbolic properties of the cocycle generated by F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf>. We apply the critical set method to show that, under some additional requirements on the derivative of the function φ, the secondary collisions compensate weakening of the hyperbolicity due to primary collisions and the cocycle generated by F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf> becomes hyperbolic in contrary to the case when secondary collisions can be partially eliminated.

articleTitle: Homoclinic transversal trajectories of singularly perturbed periodic Hamiltonian systems with disappearing separatrix
abstract: We study a Hamiltonian system with 1.5 degrees of freedom with a Hamiltonian slowly varying in time. The bifurcation parameter of the system is a twice continuously differentiable periodic function φ with simple zeros. The presence of zeros of the function φ implies existence of a cascade of pitchfork bifurcations in the phase space of the "frozen" system. In this work we obtain a sufficient condition for the existence of transversal "rotating" homoclinic trajectories of the system. The result is based on asymptotic analysis of solutions to the Cauchy problem in different domains of the phase space.

articleTitle: On semi-classical spectral series for an atom in a periodic polarized electric field
abstract: In this report we present preliminary results about the tunneling problem for a magnetic Schrödinger operator. As a motivation, we consider the 3-D time-dependent Schrödinger operator H(t) = −h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>∆ + V + E(t) • x, where V is a radial potential and E(t) is a circularly polarized field with uniform frequency ω. The quantum monodromy operator (QMO) that takes the system through a complete period T = 2π/ω, turns out to be unitarily equivalent to exp{iTP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf>(x,hD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>)/h}, where P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf>(x,hD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>)) identifies with a magnetic Schrödinger operator. When V is sufficiently confining, P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf>(x,hD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>)) presents a double magnetic well. Then we construct its semi-classical ground state and examine the splitting between its two first eigenvalues.

articleTitle: Euler–Lagrange equations for full topology optimization of the Q-factor in leaky cavities
abstract: We derive Euler–Lagrange equations for the structural optimization of exponential decay rate of standing waves in 3-D leaky optical cavities. This leads to a new class of time-harmonic differential or integro-differential equations, which can be written as nonlinear Maxwell equations with switching functions of special types. Our approach is based on the notion of Pareto optimal frontier and on the multi-parameter perturbation theory for eigenvalues.
